labelChirho: Qal: to rise, arise, get up
descriptionChirho: The basic physical sense of rising from a seated, lying, or lower position, or arising to take action; the most frequent use of qum in narrative (wayyaqom, 'and he arose') and commands (qum, 'arise!').

labelChirho: Qal: to stand firm, endure, be valid
descriptionChirho: The stative sense of remaining standing, enduring, persisting, or being valid/established; used of counsel, words, plans, or entities that remain in force (yaqum, 'it shall stand'; Arabic yathbutu, 'it is firm').

labelChirho: Qal: to rise up against, oppose
descriptionChirho: The hostile sense of rising up against an adversary, used especially in participle constructions with pronominal suffixes (qamay, 'those rising against me'); the Arabic and Swahili glosses consistently use 'oppose/rebel' terminology.

A specialized physical sense of standing motionless or congealing (of waters or fluids that become solid/fixed), as in the Song of the Sea (Exod 15:8) where the waters 'stood still' (Arabic jamuda/jamidatan).

labelChirho: Hifil: to raise up a person
descriptionChirho: The causative sense of raising up a person — a deliverer, prophet, king, shepherd, or enemy — bringing them onto the stage of history; glossed as 'raise up' (Spanish levantar, Arabic aqama, Korean ileukhida).

labelChirho: Hifil: to set up, erect (physical object)
descriptionChirho: The causative sense of physically erecting or setting up a structure such as a pillar, altar, tabernacle, or monument; glossed as 'erected/set up' (Spanish erigir, Arabic aqama, Swahili kusimamisha).

The causative-abstract sense of establishing, confirming, or upholding a covenant, kingdom, throne, or decree; glossed as 'establish/confirm' (Spanish establecer/confirmar, Arabic uqimu/yuthabbitu, Swahili kuimarisha/kuthibitisha).

The causative sense emphasizing the realization or fulfillment of a spoken word, promise, or oath; glossed specifically as 'fulfill' (Spanish cumplir, Arabic aqama in fulfillment context, Swahili kutimiza).

labelChirho: Hifil: to rouse, stir up from inactivity
descriptionChirho: The causative sense of rousing or stirring someone from sleep or inactivity; glossed as 'rouse him' (Spanish despertar/levantar, Arabic yunhiduhu/yuqimuhu, Swahili kuamsha).

The intensive stem expressing thorough confirmation, establishment, or fulfillment of words, oaths, or statutes; glossed as 'confirm/establish' (Spanish confirmar/establecer, Arabic yuthabbitu, Swahili kuthibitisha).

labelChirho: Hofal: to be raised up, be established
descriptionChirho: The passive of the Hifil, expressing being raised up or being established/fulfilled by an external agent; glossed as 'was raised/established' (Spanish fue levantado/exaltado, Arabic uqima/al-muqam).

labelChirho: Hitpael: to rise up against, set oneself against
descriptionChirho: The reflexive-reciprocal stem expressing hostile rising or self-opposition against another; used of adversaries and enemies who set themselves against someone (Spanish adversario/los que se levantan contra, Arabic mutamarridin/qa'imin).
